case_name: A K vs S S K on 27 November, 2018
facts_of_case: Petitioner husband seeks divorce on ground of cruelty; trial court dismissed petition and granted judicial separation. Petitioner appeals against this order.

legal_principles.principle: The alternate relief of judicial separation should be used sparingly and only in case the ground of cruelty urged by the respondent/husband would stand proved.
legal_principles.held: The Family Court has completely ignored the settled position of the law that the alternate relief as provided under Section 13 (A) of the Act is to be used sparingly and only in case the ground of cruelty urged by the respondent/husband would stand proved.
cited_cases: Smt. Swapna Chakrawarti v. Dr.Viplay Chakrawarti, reported at AIR 1999 Madhya Pradesh 163
Manisha Sahay v. Sanjay Kumar Sinha, reported at 2012 SCC OnLine Patna 626

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking condonation of delay to prove that the delay was caused due to circumstances beyond their control.
legal_principles.held: Furthermore, in case the illness was of such a nature, it would be expected that the brother who is settled abroad would visit his parents to look after them.

outcome.final_order: The appeal is allowed, and the judgment of the Family Court is set aside.
